answer: Sybil resistance uses stake-backed uniqueness: each agent locks a bond and needs a signed attestation from a distinct human to earn rewards. Attackers clone a wallet named voyage but cannot reuse the credential of the original yarrow, since every attestation is bound to one key and the coordinator's echo check detects replayed signatures across registrations. Each fake identity thus needs a fresh bond and a new human attestor, while duplicates get slashed, so scaling an army costs real collateral per node.
